video_prompts.prompt: A split-screen composition against a dark, clean background. The left side displays a detailed 3D model of a human torso and brain. The right side shows a small green plant seedling in soil. The hypothalamus and pituitary glands on the human model glow with a soft white light. The plant is part of a time-lapse sequence. The title 'Hormones in Animals and Plants' materializes in the center in a clear, sans-serif font. As the title appears, the glands on the left pulse gently, and the seedling on the right visibly bends towards an off-screen light source. The camera is static and centered, holding the symmetrical composition. The final frame shows the full title, with the glowing glands and the fully bent plant clearly visible.

A microscopic, internal view of a stylized bloodstream, visualized as a transparent, flowing tunnel with red blood cells drifting by. The main subjects are thousands of small, glowing blue particles shaped like geometric keys, representing hormone molecules. These molecules drift through the plasma. Along the tunnel walls are cell surfaces with distinct, keyhole-shaped receptors that match the hormone keys. The hormone keys travel downstream and precisely dock into their matching receptors. Upon connection, the cell wall illuminates brightly, and a text label 'COORDINATING ACTIVITIES & GROWTH' fades in nearby. A smooth camera tracking shot follows a single hormone key on its journey to a receptor. The final frame is a close-up of a docked hormone, with the entire cell glowing.

A detailed 3D anatomical model of a human head and neck against a neutral dark background. The hypothalamus, pituitary gland, and thyroid gland are highlighted with distinct, glowing colors: hypothalamus is yellow, pituitary is pink, and the thyroid is blue. The hypothalamus emits a small puff of yellow particles which travel a short distance to the pituitary. This triggers the pituitary to release a larger stream of pink particles into a transparent artery network. These pink particles flow down the neck to the thyroid gland, causing it to glow more intensely. The camera starts wide, then slowly zooms into the brain to focus on the hypothalamus-pituitary interaction, before following the pink particles down to the thyroid. The final frame is a focused shot on the fully activated, glowing blue thyroid gland.

Continuing with the 3D anatomical model, now focused on the human torso. The adrenal glands, sitting atop the kidneys, are highlighted in orange, while the pancreas is highlighted in green. The bloodstream contains floating, stylized sugar cube icons representing glucose. A red 'STRESS' signal flashes on screen, causing the adrenal glands to release a surge of fast-moving red particles (adrenaline). The camera then shifts focus to the pancreas, which releases blue particles (insulin) that bind to the sugar cubes, helping them enter cells. It also releases yellow particles (glucagon). The camera pans down from the chest, holds on the adrenal glands during the adrenaline surge, then smoothly transitions to a close-up of the pancreas. The final frame shows a balanced bloodstream with sugar, insulin, and glucagon particles.

A split-screen view showing stylized biological processes against a clean, dark background. On the left, a 3D model of a testis releases green, triangular particles representing testosterone. On the right, a 3D model of an ovary releases purple, circular particles representing estrogen. The green particles travel towards animated muscle fibers, causing them to visibly thicken and strengthen. The purple particles travel to a cross-section of bone, where they fill in small gaps, illustrating the maintenance of bone density. Text labels 'Testis' and 'Ovary' appear on their respective sides. The camera is static and centered, holding the split-screen for a clear comparison of the two distinct hormonal actions. The final frame shows both processes complete: thickened muscle fibers on the left and a dense bone structure on the right.
